result_text:
`analyzeLandscape` now runs the same code as `updateLandscape`, with the same options. The `cli` module compiles. I didn't run any tests, and I didn't run the new command against a real analysis root.

- **`Commands.java`:** I added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE` and its description. The description says it is the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands and the same as `updateLandscape`. `analyzeLandscape` is also listed in the no-argument usage overview, next to `updateLandscape`.
- **`CommandLineInterface.java`:** `run` dispatches both names to the existing `updateLandscape(args)` method. `-help` prints usage under the name the user typed, with that command's own description.
- **`README.md`:** it had no command descriptions, so I added a short "Command line" section. It lists `init`, `generateReports`, `analyzeLandscape`, `updateLandscape` (noted as the same command, kept for existing scripts) and `updateConfig`.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the command list now shows `analyzeLandscape` with `updateLandscape` as its alias. You didn't ask for this.
